text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000215 bills 99215 far above expectation, including on one-condition patients, but the few charts reviewed support the billed levels, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess 99215 share is not confined to sicker patients: it is elevated in every complexity band, most notably among one-condition patients, where the rate is several times the all-provider rate. Sampled examples such as C0103811 (hyperlipidemia only), C0104225 (hypertension only) and C0103752 (no chronic conditions) look hard to reconcile with high-complexity decision-making on their face, which is consistent with upcoding. Against that, none of the 7 documented 99215 claims, including C0103927, fell below the billed level. Only 2 of the moderate-plus data-reviewed notes lacked a lab or test line, so there is little sign of inflated notes. However, records cover under 5% of claims and only 7 at 99215, too few to rule out a problem or to show the high share is justified. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims (for example C0103818, C0104027, C0104148) and check whether the documented MDM reflects real complexity or templated or cloned text."}
